steps.label: Priority
steps.sub: a QoS tag lets some jobs jump the queue

steps.label: Fair-share
steps.sub: recent usage lowers your effective priority over time

steps.label: Preemption
steps.sub: a lower-priority job can be suspended to free resources

eyebrow: Slurm: QoS and fair-share in practice
code:
# Submit with an explicit QoS
sbatch --qos=high --partition=gpu --gres=gpu:1 train.sh

# Check your current fair-share factor
sshare -u $USER -a
caption: Fair-share tracks each user's recent usage so one sweep can't perpetually dominate the queue.

code:
apiVersion: scheduling.k8s.io/v1
kind: PriorityClass
metadata:
  name: high-priority-research
value: 1000
preemptionPolicy: PreemptLowerPriority
caption: A higher-priority pod can preempt a lower-priority one, which is then automatically requeued.

subtitle: The scheduler decides whose job runs -- this is about deciding which experiments deserve to be run at all.
